$comment: sha256 of every migration file that has ALREADY been applied to a real database.
D1 records applied migrations by FILENAME in d1_migrations, so a migration that
has run is skipped on every later `wrangler d1 migrations apply` — silently, with
no warning. Editing a shipped migration is therefore not a no-op in the repository
and a no-op in production: the code starts naming a column the database does not
have, and every statement that names it fails at runtime.
That is not hypothetical. `songs.reader_version` was added by editing 0001, so the
column never reached the live database, `applyMetadata` and `upsertFileFacts` both
failed against it, and a library of 80 albums served empty artists, albums, genres,
and search while 489 tests passed. See migrations/0002_songs_reader_version.sql.
RULE: a migration in this file must never change again. To change the schema, add a
new numbered file and add it here in the same commit. `test/schema.int.test.ts`
asserts both directions — every file on disk is listed, and every listed hash
matches — so an edit fails the suite instead of the deployment.
